entries.topic: What a good product listing contains
entries.content: A listing needs a short title naming the object and its material, three to five lines describing size, material and how it was made, and clear photographs in daylight against a plain background.
Work out the cost of materials, then add a fair value for your hours, then add packing and postage. Selling below material cost plus your time is a loss even when it feels like a sale.

Some Indian crafts carry a Geographical Indication (GI) tag which identifies where they were made. Only producers registered under that GI may use the name. Do not claim a GI you are not registered for.

entries.topic: Photographing a product on a phone
entries.content: Shoot in indirect daylight near a window, not under a tube light and not in direct sun. Use a plain cloth or sheet of paper as background. Take one photo of the whole object and two close-ups of detail.
